what: The pages under You, one route so a push or a link opens any of them: payouts, insights (Insights: the week chart, your things, how they are doing, by site, worth, goal), records, connections (Your sites), rules (Rules and limits), log (Activity), notifications, defaults (App defaults), permissions (Permissions: what the agent may do), settings. A linked site's own page is app/behavior/you/connections/[site].json.

frame.who: The person clearing out reaches Payouts and Your sites after a sale or a sign-out; the person holding a minimum checks Rules and limits for their lowest; the flipper reads By site and Records; anyone leaving uses Settings.
frame.how_often: Rarely, each one: a page is opened to change one thing or check one number, then left.
frame.came_to: Change one setting or limit, link a site, undo one automatic step, or download the year's sales.
frame.costly_mistake: A price set without the person's tap (limits end in Approve); a rule turned on before the person approved it three times without a change (its switch is disabled and says why); deleting an account while a sale is open (refused, and says so). Accepting an offer from the lock screen without the owner's face: Accept, Approve and Counter always need Face ID, and that row has no switch.
frame.ways_out: spec/ways-out.md: Pause selling (away mode where a site has one, end and bring back elsewhere, never relisting on Poshmark), never suggest photo edits, units and currency, delete (refused while a sale is open), a site's 2FA or captcha (Try again or leave it), unlink a site (Undo for a few seconds). Notifications: every kind can be switched off, quiet hours (a deadline inside them is sent before they start), Group by item.
frame.in_the_loop: Rules and limits is where the hand-off line is drawn and moved: what runs alone with a switch, what always asks without one, and each item's lowest price, saved only on Approve. Activity shows every automatic step with Undo while it can be undone where it happened. Your sites puts every place a site and our record disagree first, each with Open on the site, so the person can check the site itself. Permissions lists every kind of step as On its own (with Undo), Asks first, Always asks or Never; a person can make any kind more careful there, and a kind runs on its own only after 3 unedited approvals, under Rules and limits.

back: Back goes to the screen it came from; opened directly, it goes to You.
decisions: One route for every page under You, so a push or a link opens any directly (spec/pages.md §1, rule 2); each page is its own file in app/src/you/.
By site, worth and the goal share one page: three short subjects that fit in under three screens (spec/pages.md §1, rule 4).
Sites are their logos with their state in words, never their names in words (C5); every row runs on its own, so one sign-in never blocks the rest (Ben, 03:22).
The demo's first Link on Mercari stops at the site's code step and times out, so the error and Try again can be seen and tested; the second try links.
A rule can be switched on only once it has 3 unedited approvals; below that its switch is disabled and its line says the count (decisions: tiers that learn; only unedited approvals count).
The floor and the always-accept line are the agent's guesses until the person changes them, so they show as Guess fields (dotted), and they save only on Approve: a price is never set without a tap.
The ceiling here is the always-accept line: above it an offer is taken at once, below the floor it always asks. The buyer's ceiling (most you'd pay) belongs to Want and Buy.
Delete account is refused while a sale is open, as deleting an item is (ways-out, Delete it); otherwise it says what ends first and waits for Approve.
Pause selling picks a date two weeks out as its guess, shown as a Guess field the person can change.
Records keeps its foot button for the CSV: the one act on the page, labelled a record.

A sale's money moves through four words, Sold, On its way, Ready on the site, In your bank, each with its date (spec/edge-cases.md, Ben 05:05). A row says the word it is at and the next with its date; a date the site does not give is said in words (after you ship, when you cash out), never guessed. The per-site clocks are research/price/nate/fees-and-taxes.md and edge-cases, in app/src/you/money-steps.ts until spec/sites.mjs has payout rows.
Money stays On its way until it is in the bank or in the hand, so ready-on-the-site money is not counted as paid out; You and Payouts use the same sum.
Local pickup is paid in hand, so its money has two words: Sold, then In your hand.

Instant payout is offered only where the site has one, only once the money is ready on the site, with its fee in the label, as a second-kind button under the free date: never the default (edge-cases, Instant payout costs money).
A payout row opens the four words in a sheet rather than the item: the row is about the money; the item is one tap further, See the item.

Your sites audits every site from one app (Ben 05:18): anything where a site and our record disagree goes on top across every site, each with Open on the site, so the person checks the site itself rather than our copy. A linked site's row opens its page (app/behavior/you/connections/[site].json), where Unlink now lives.

A mismatch is worked out, never stored: a write whose read-back differs from the listing (we ended it and it still shows; we posted it and it doesn't), a listing the site refused or kept, a step that didn't take, or a site_changed_listing card (app/src/you/site-audit.ts).

Notifications is its own page (spec/notifications.md, Ben 05:23): each kind with a switch and one example of what it would say, under the level it is sent at, Right away or In the next summary; what is never sent is listed with no switch, so the line shows.

A kind's level is fixed by spec/notifications.md's defaults; the switch turns it on or off. Moving a kind between levels is left for later: the spec's fallback (3 ignored pushes move a kind to the summary) does it without a control.

Accept, Approve and Counter from the lock screen always need Face ID: they commit the person to a sale or a meeting, so that row has a value and no switch (spec/notifications.md, Acting from the lock screen).
Quiet hours move from Settings to Notifications and are on by default, 10 pm to 8 am, as the spec sets; a deadline inside them is sent before they start.
Messages and addresses stay off the lock screen until the person turns them on, because a phone on a table is seen by others.

App defaults and permission defaults (Ben 05:47) are two pages under Settings, not sections of it, so Settings stays one screen and each page is about one thing: what a new listing starts from, and what the agent may do.

Permission defaults live once, on Permissions; Rules and limits links to it instead of repeating the kinds that always ask, and keeps what is learned (rules after 3 approvals) and each item's lowest price. Why: one fact in one place, and the learned rules are a different question from the starting modes.

A kind can be made more careful on Permissions, never less: a kind that starts by asking is not offered On its own there, because running alone is earned by 3 unedited approvals (decisions: tiers that learn).

Locked kinds (a price under your lowest, sharing your address, refunds and payment, claims that it is genuine) show as Always asks with no control; taking a deal off the site shows as Never (spec/product.md §5).
Taking a listing down after it sells stays On its own with no control, and its row says why: so it can't sell twice.

App defaults start from spec: Sell it, the lowest price suggested from sold prices and set by the person, Clean up on and Enhance with AI off, replies in the person's voice, ship or pickup from their limits, the saved pickup spot, and only linked sites as default sites.

Every page draws loading, failed and offline from ?state= (app/src/demo/screen.ts) the same way, through app/src/you/page-status.tsx: gray shapes, Couldn’t load with Try again, or the last copy under Waiting for signal. Your sites draws loading and failed on a site's row instead, since one site signing in never blocks the page.
A page that lists every setting from the start (Settings, Notifications, App defaults, Permissions) skips empty and one, with why.

App defaults holds the account's cross-listing price rule, Same take-home unless the person switches it (decisions.md, 2026-11-15: cross-listing starts on same take-home). Each rule is its name and its one plain reason from SPREADS; the numbers for one jacket sit a tap under them (Ben 06:53: "in plain language ... then see numbers if need be"), priced by the engine's own sitePrice. One item's own rule is set on its Plan, not here.

Insights holds the analytics that left You (Ben, 10:27: "profile shouldnt have analytics"): the week chart, Your things and How they're doing come first, then By site, worth and the goal. Activity opens from Rules and limits, and Records from Settings, so nothing that was on You is more than one row away.
